summary.headline: BEL H1 FY27 revenue rose 25.97% to INR 12,824 mn; order book INR 68,717 mn, with guidance of 15%+ growth reaffirmed.
summary.overview: Bharat Electronics reported H1 FY27 (Q1+Q2 combined) revenue from operations of INR 12,824 mn, up 25.97% YoY, with PBT of INR 3,467 mn (+14.66%) and PAT of INR 2,589 mn (+14.80%). Management said EPS rose to INR 3.54 from INR 3.09 and EBITDA growth was 27.43%. Order book stood at INR 68,717 mn as of 1 October 2026, with INR 7,334 mn of orders won in FY27 to that date. The company kept its full-year guidance unchanged despite the strong H1, as it expects a more even quarterly execution profile and the timing of large orders (QRSAM, NGC) remains uncertain.

segments.name: Defence electronics (core)
segments.commentary: Management said the defence to non-defence mix is typically 90:10. Top order-book projects as of 1 Oct: Electronic business INR 4,200 mn, LCA Mk1 INR 3,200 mn, LRSAM INR 2,900 mn, BMP-2 upgrade INR 2,600 mn, Ashwini radar INR 2,500 mn, Mi-17 EW suite INR 2,200 mn, one export order INR 1,700 mn.

segments.name: Cyber / civilian
segments.commentary: Network and Cyber Security SBU (created about 2.5 years ago) is executing civilian cybersecurity orders of roughly INR 400-500 mn, with a pipeline the company describes as potentially thousands of mn.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 15%+ (annual report range 15-20%); management said H1's 26% growth is partly due to deliberately smoothing quarterly output and any upside would be a positive surprise.
FY27 order inflow guided at minimum INR 25,000 mn excluding QRSAM and INR 55,000 mn including QRSAM; management reiterated these figures.
EBITDA margin guided at around 28%; R&D investment about INR 2,200 mn; capex about INR 1,200 mn.

NGC sub-system orders from GSL and GRSE expected to be placed in a staggered way within about 6 months, mostly before FY27 close; management said roughly INR 15,000 mn of these is expected, with a possible 1-2 line items slipping.
QRSAM order expected shortly, possibly at the next CCS meeting; management said it is more than 99% confident of award to BEL.
Management said the P-75I order may slip to next year; Shatrughat, Samaghat and HAMMER are expected before March.
capex_capacity: Combined IR and RF seeker capacity of over 1,000 units per year, scalable 2-3x; new IR seeker factory at Nimmaluru near Machilipatnam is I4.0 compliant.
Tamil Nadu Explosives Ltd is now wholly owned by BEL; hot integration facility for missiles is operational, with ammunition manufacturing not in-house.
Development order for airborne radar (for Su-30/LCA) with LRDE; production orders expected around FY28-FY29.
Ground Based Mobile ELINT system (INR 1,261 mn) and low-level lightweight radar (INR 770 mn) orders from Indian Army; company said execution will be quick.
Counter-drone: high-end systems with hard kill; microwave DEW being added via in-house and DRDO efforts; working with 6-8 start-ups on drones.
demand_pricing: Management said margins are similar between nomination and competitive orders; nomination orders originated as multi-vendor competitions where BEL was L1.
AMCA bid submitted in consortium with L&T (50:50, L&T as lead); management expects technical evaluation of 2-3 months and hopes for L1 before March.

Next Generation Corvette: GSL and GRSE contracts signed; total programme size reported by an analyst as increasing from about INR 38,000 mn to INR 53,000 mn, which management did not dispute directly.
QRSAM: management said escalation is unlikely given the government process; the expected order value remains about INR 250,000 mn; about 70% of orders to flow to 200+ MSME partners.
Missiles: BEL is DCPP partner for LRLACM and Pralay; management said missile electronics are 60-70% of missile cost and seekers 20-30%.

qa_highlights.question: When will the QRSAM order come and could private players take a share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the order is expected very shortly, possibly at the next CCS, and it is more than 99% confident of award to BEL; private entry is seen as a future possibility, not for this order.

qa_highlights.question: Would FY27 guidance be upgraded given 26% H1 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management kept 15-20% (more than 15%) guidance, saying H1 growth reflects smoothing of quarterly output and it expects Q4 productivity to be normally higher.

qa_highlights.question: Is the QRSAM delay affecting execution and what is the timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has started proactive work on QT and FOPM, and expects to recover a few months after order award; the delay was internally expected to be around August-September.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a breakup of the order book and what is expected in H2 order inflow?
qa_highlights.answer: Top projects are listed as above; management expects NGC, QRSAM, Shatrughat, Samaghat and HAMMER as key H2 orders, with P-75I possibly slipping to next year.

qa_highlights.question: Will NGC orders be incremental to the base INR 25,000 mn?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NGC is included in the INR 25,000 mn excluding QRSAM target; if all NGC orders arrive before March, the company will cross that target by a large margin.

qa_highlights.question: Does BEL supply BrahMos seekers and what is the seeker capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: BEL is not yet in BrahMos seekers but supplies IR and RF seekers for Akash, Astra and others; combined capacity is over 1,000 units, scalable 2-3x.

risks_watch: Timing of QRSAM (INR 250,000 mn), NGC and other large awards; management acknowledged possible slippage of 1-2 line items and P-75I possibly moving to FY28.
Sustainability of H1 execution (26% growth) versus 15-20% full-year guidance and BEL's stated plan to smooth quarterly delivery.
Order book described as lower YoY per analyst question; FY27 order inflow depends heavily on NGC.
Competitive intensity from private players (Adani Defence, L&T in AMCA consortium) in radars, EW and missiles.
No escalation expected on QRSAM despite cost increases since the original INR estimate; execution may need to absorb cost inflation.
Detector technology for EOIR remains partly dependent on DRDO.
summary.management_tone: Confident and reassuring on guidance and order timing, with repeated assurances that all targets will be met. Evasive on specifics such as ELINT deployment, EW export potential, IACCS upgrade and exact NGC timing, citing strategic confidentiality.
key_quotes: We are going to meet our guidance given at the start of the year.
So this program, as of now and more than 99%, I am confident it is coming to us very soon.
And then we have submitted our bid based on the RFP issued to us.
